data.narrative: Built a JWT-based auth surface (public redirect vs protected admin API), scoped link access to the owner with fail-closed 404 semantics, enforced a per-principal/IP rate-limit matrix, and closed the injected Module 04 BREAK loop: the login rate-limit guard had been stubbed out with allowed=True, so I restored the check_rate_limit call (10/min per IP), re-ran the full suite (28 passed), and recorded the security lesson - guards only protect when they actually run.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose JWT (short 15-min TTL) over API keys because this is a public consumer service: short-lived signed tokens expire fast when leaked and scale to real login flows, versus static long-lived keys that carry no built-in expiry.
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE module_04 choice B with reasoning recorded; config enforces JWT_SECRET >= 32 chars and TTL in [1,1440].

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced the injected login-limit failure via the failing regression tests (20 logins with no 429s), root-caused it to the stubbed allowed=True in auth.py, restored the rate-limit call, and confirmed with the full suite green.

Identified that the real vulnerability was a guard that never runs - unlimited credential brute force - and that JWT expiry/verification only protects when the guard is actually invoked. Also enforces a strong-secret validator so weak JWT secrets fail fast at startup.
dimension_scores.evidence: auth.py now calls check_rate_limit('login', client_ip, login_rate_per_min) returning 429; config.py rejects 'replace-me-locally' and secrets < 32 chars.

dimension_scores.observation: Separated the public hot path (/r) from a protected admin surface, scoped enumeration to the caller with indistinguishable 404s, and applied a per-principal/per-IP rate-limit matrix (login/create/redirect/analytics) matching the public-consumer abuse-first constraints.
dimension_scores.evidence: Owner-scoped list/get (404 for foreign links), rate limits on login (10/min/IP), create-link (30/min/user), redirect (120/min/IP).

dimension_scores.observation: Documented the auth decision, the owner-scoping contract, the rate-limit matrix, and the BREAK/FIX lesson in a concise evidence file with concrete status-code proof.
dimension_scores.evidence: progress/evidence/module-04/evidence.txt records 200/401/404/429 behaviors with exact limits.

strengths: Applied the failure-first drill live: reproduced the login brute-force symptom (20 successes, zero 429s) before touching code.
Root-caused the bug to a guard that never runs (allowed=True) rather than patching the symptom.
Closed the loop with regression: full suite green (28 passed) plus evidence file recording the rate-limit contract.
Chose JWT with short TTL and enforced a strong-secret config validator - security by construction.
data.recommendation: Next module: harden error handling and structured logging so failures carry correlation IDs and consistent error contracts across the public and admin surfaces.

public_evidence.student_action: Restored and verified the login rate-limit guard (10/min/IP) that had been stubbed out, returning 429 with Retry-After when exceeded.
public_evidence.technical_detail: app/routers/auth.py calls check_rate_limit('login', client_ip, settings.login_rate_per_min) before credential verification.
public_evidence.proof: pytest -q: 28 passed; login burst shows 10x 200 then 429.
public_evidence.ability: Rate limiting as a brute-force defense
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the login path is throttled - a live credential-stuffing defense that many production APIs ship without.

public_evidence.student_action: Scoped link create/list/get to the authenticated owner with fail-closed 404s so foreign links are indistinguishable from missing ones.
public_evidence.technical_detail: app/deps.py decode_access_token -> get_current_user; links_service.get_link filters Link.created_by == owner.
public_evidence.proof: Bob GET /links/{alice_id} returns 404; Alice GET returns 200.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Hides resource existence to the caller - an IDOR-resistant pattern for multi-tenant public APIs.

concepts_demonstrated.concept: JWT short-TTL auth over API keys

teaching_approaches.detail: stubbed guard reproduced live then restored
